name: Sacred Temples of Kerala
theme: Kerala's great living shrines — Shiva, the Goddess, Vishnu and Ayyappa — in the distinctive temple architecture of the Malabar coast
description: Kerala's temples speak a language all their own: circular and square sanctums crowned with steep copper-clad roofs, timber theatre-halls, lamp-lined courtyards, and murals painted in mineral colours. This circuit gathers the state's most revered shrines, from the hills to the sea. Shiva is honoured at Vaikom; at Ettumanoor, famed for its classical murals; at Kaduthuruthy, which completes the Vaikathashtami trio; and at Vadakkunnathan, the circular laterite-and-timber archetype crowning Thrissur's hill. The Mother Goddess appears at Chottanikkara, at Attukal, whose Pongala draws vast crowds, and at ancient Kodungallur. Vishnu is worshipped as the child Krishna at Guruvayur and Ambalappuzha, as Arjuna's charioteer at Aranmula on the Pamba, and reclining upon the serpent Ananta at Padmanabhaswamy in Thiruvananthapuram. And high in the forested Western Ghats stands Sabarimala, the hill shrine of Ayyappa, drawing one of the largest annual pilgrimages on earth. Together they trace the devotional and artistic world of Kerala.
